280: 	 * <li><code>/foo/bar/image-5</code></li>
281: 	 * <li><code>/foo/bar/image-6</code></li>
282: 	 * <li><code>/foo/bar/image-7</code></li>
283: 	 * <li><code>/foo/bar/image-8</code></li>
284: 	 * </ol>
285: 	 * <p>
286: 	 * and so on.
287: 	 * </p>
288: 	 *
289: 	 * @param dir			The directory in which the files are to be located.
290: 	 * @param format		The format string to use.
291: 	 * @param start			The value from which to start counting.
292:  	 * @throws IOException	If the specified directory path is not a directory,
293:  	 * 						or if does not exist.
294: 	 */
295: 	public ConsecutivelyNumberedFilenames(File dir, String format, int start) throws IOException {
296: 		checkDirectory(dir);
297: 		this.iter = new ConsecutivelyNumberedFilenamesIterator(dir, format, start);
298: 	}
299: 
300: 	private static void checkDirectory(File dir) throws IOException {
301: 		if (!dir.isDirectory()) {
302: 			throw new IOException(
303: 					"Specified path is not a directory or does not exist."
304: 			);
305: 		}
306: 	}
307: 
308: 	private static class ConsecutivelyNumberedFilenamesIterator implements Iterator<File> {
309: 		private final File dir;
310: 		private final String format;
311: 		private int count;
312: 		
313: 		public ConsecutivelyNumberedFilenamesIterator(File dir, String format, int start) {
314: 			super();
315: 			this.dir = dir;
316: 			this.format = format;
317: 			this.count = start;
318: 		}
319: 
320: 		public boolean hasNext() {
321: 			return true;
322: 		}
323: 
324: 		public File next() {
325: 			File f = new File(dir, String.format(format, count));
326: 			count++;
327: 			return f;
328: 		}
329: 
330: 		public void remove() {
331: 			throw new UnsupportedOperationException(
332: 					"Cannot remove elements from this iterator."
333: 			);
334: 		}
335: 	}
336: 
337: 	/**
338: 	 * Returns an iterator which generates file names according to the rules
339: 	 * specified by this object.
340: 	 * 
341: 	 * @return		An iterator which generates file names.
342: 	 */
343: 	public Iterator<File> iterator() {
344: 		return iter;
345: 	}
346: }
